hints: Find the time to reach the highest point under gravity: $v = u - gt = 0 \implies 40 - 10t = 0$.
By symmetry, if the particle is above the building for $4\text{ s}$, it spends $2\text{ s}$ ascending above the roof and $2\text{ s}$ descending back to the roof level.
The time taken to reach the top of the building is $t = 4 - 2 = 2\text{ s}$. Evaluate $s = ut - \frac{1}{2}gt^2$ at $t = 2\text{ s}$.
walkthrough:
Find the time to reach the highest point ($v = 0$, $u = 40\text{ m s}^{-1}$, $a = -10\text{ m s}^{-2}$):
$$0 = 40 - 10t_{\text{top}} \implies t_{\text{top}} = 4\text{ s}$$

Since the particle is above the roof level for $4\text{ s}$, by vertical motion symmetry it reaches the roof at:
$$t = t_{\text{top}} - \frac{4}{2} = 4 - 2 = 2\text{ s}$$

Calculate the height $h$ of the building using $s = ut - \frac{1}{2}gt^2$ at $t = 2\text{ s}$:
$$h = 40(2) - \frac{1}{2}(10)(2^2) = 80 - 20 = 60\text{ m}$$

ai_rubric.Modelling Vertical Motion: Finds highest point at $t = 4\text{ s}$, deduces time to roof is $t = 2\text{ s}$ (or $6\text{ s}$), and calculates $h = 60\text{ m}$.

teacher_walkthrough:
Find the time taken for the particle to reach maximum height, where vertical velocity is momentarily zero:
$$v = u - gt$$
$$0 = 40 - 10t_{\text{top}}$$
$$10t_{\text{top}} = 40 \implies t_{\text{top}} = 4\text{ s}$$

By the symmetry of free fall under gravity, the time spent above any given horizontal level is bisected by the time at maximum height. Since the particle is above the top of the building for a duration of $4\text{ s}$, it spends $2\text{ s}$ rising from the top of the building to the peak, and $2\text{ s}$ falling back down to the top of the building.

Therefore, the particle passes the top of the building on the way up at time:
$$t_1 = 4 - 2 = 2\text{ s}$$

Use the displacement equation with $u = 40\text{ m s}^{-1}$, $a = -10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, and $t = 2\text{ s}$:
$$s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2$$
$$h = 40(2) - \frac{1}{2}(10)(2^2)$$
$$h = 80 - 5(4) = 80 - 20 = 60\text{ m}$$

hints: Write the height of the first particle above the ground at time $t$: $h_1(t) = 40t - 5t^2$.
The second particle is projected from height $60\text{ m}$ at time $t = 1\text{ s}$ with speed $20\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Write its height above ground: $h_2(t) = 60 + 20(t - 1) - 5(t - 1)^2$.
walkthrough:
Express the height of the first particle above ground level at time $t$:
$$h_1(t) = 40t - \frac{1}{2}(10)t^2 = 40t - 5t^2$$

Express the height of the second particle projected from the roof ($60\text{ m}$) at $t = 1\text{ s}$:
$$h_2(t) = 60 + 20(t - 1) - 5(t - 1)^2$$
$$h_2(t) = 60 + 20t - 20 - 5(t^2 - 2t + 1) = 40 + 20t - 5t^2 + 10t - 5 = 35 + 30t - 5t^2$$

Set $h_1(t) = h_2(t)$ to find the time they reach the same height:
$$40t - 5t^2 = 35 + 30t - 5t^2$$
$$40t = 35 + 30t$$
$$10t = 35 \implies t = 3.5\text{ s}$$

ai_rubric.Modelling Vertical Motion: Equates $40t - 5t^2 = 60 + 20(t - 1) - 5(t - 1)^2$ and solves to obtain $t = 3.5\text{ s}$.

teacher_walkthrough: Set up coordinate expressions for the heights of both particles above the ground at time $t$ seconds after the first particle is projected.

First particle:
Initial position $y_0 = 0$, initial upward velocity $u = 40\text{ m s}^{-1}$, acceleration $a = -g = -10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$h_1(t) = 40t - \frac{1}{2}(10)t^2 = 40t - 5t^2$$

Second particle:
Projected $1\text{ s}$ later (active for duration $t - 1$), from the roof at height $y_0 = 60\text{ m}$, with initial upward velocity $u = 20\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$h_2(t) = 60 + 20(t - 1) - \frac{1}{2}(10)(t - 1)^2$$
Expand the terms:
$$h_2(t) = 60 + 20t - 20 - 5(t^2 - 2t + 1)$$
$$h_2(t) = 40 + 20t - 5t^2 + 10t - 5$$
$$h_2(t) = 35 + 30t - 5t^2$$

Add $5t^2$ to both sides to eliminate the quadratic terms:
$$40t = 35 + 30t$$

Subtract $30t$ from both sides:
$$10t = 35$$
Divide by $10$:
$$t = 3.5\text{ s}$$
